title: ChronoTE: Crosstalk-Aware Timing Estimation for Routing Optimization via Edge-Enhanced GNNs
problem: Accurate timing estimation during routing is critical but challenging at advanced nodes due to crosstalk effects. Existing estimation methods are overly pessimistic because they consider coupling capacitance alone without accounting for relative signal arrival times affecting crosstalk-induced delay.
motivation: Accurate sign-off quality delay estimation during early global routing can significantly accelerate design closure and reduce chip area by enabling better routing optimization decisions.
method: ChronoTE is an edge-enhanced graph neural network framework that performs crosstalk-aware net delay estimation by jointly modeling physical topology and timing characteristics. The approach embeds timing-window-aware features into edge representations to enable accurate delay prediction without requiring full routing or parasitic extraction.
key_novelty: Edge-enhanced GNN framework incorporating timing-window-aware features for accurate crosstalk-aware delay prediction during early routing stages without full parasitic extraction.
contributions: Novel edge-enhanced GNN architecture with timing-window-aware feature embedding
Crosstalk-aware delay estimation considering both capacitance and signal timing relationships
Sign-off quality predictions achievable in early global routing stage
Demonstrated area reduction and design closure acceleration on industrial-scale open-source designs
limitations: Evaluation only on open-source designs; applicability to proprietary commercial tools and very advanced nodes (3nm and below) is not demonstrated.
